newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thailand exports March NGL amid excess supplies.
newsitem.headline: Thailand exports March NGL amid excess supplies.

text.p: State-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) has started exporting natural gas liquids (NGL) by tender to sell excess supplies, industry sources said on Thursday.
PTT awarded a tender to sell 90,000 barrels of NGL lifting in March at 50 cents over Singapore naphtha quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to Singapore.
The tender, to sell the three 30,000-barrel cargoes from Sri Racha, which closed February 24, was awarded to a Japanese trader for gasoline blending in Singapore, sources said.
They said PTT started to tender NGL sales in February, selling two cargoes at a "slightly lower price" than in the latest tender.
PTT sources said it has exported NGL in the past if it had an excess of supply. However, it did not export any last year.

Exports started this month due to an excess of NGL with the start-up in January of a new gas separation plant No.3 at Sri Racha, which processes natural gas into liquid petroleum gas (LPG), NGL, methane and ethane.
Industry sources also said domestic refiner Thai Oil Co Ltd had reduced the volume of NGL it takes from Sri Racha because it is using an alternative blending component for gasoline.
PTT sources could not say whether it would issue a tender for April, saying that it would depend on Thai Oil's requirements.
